}} '''Real Sociedad de Fútbol, S.A.D.''', commonly known as '''La Real''' or '''Real Sociedad''' ({{IPA|es|reˈal soθjeˈðað|pron}} {{IPA|es||lang|Forvo.com Pronunciation of Real Sociedad.ogg}};{{cite web | url=https://forvo.com/word/real_sociedad/ | title=Real Sociedad pronunciation: How to pronounce Real Sociedad in Spanish | access-date=2024-03-22 | archive-date=2024-03-22 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240322120824/https://forvo.com/word/real_sociedad/ | url-status=live }} {{lit|Royal Society}}) in English and '''Erreala''' or '''Reala''' in [[Basque language|Basque]], is a Spanish professional sports club based in the city of [[San Sebastián]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]]. The club was founded on 7 September 1909 and is best known for its [[football team]], which plays home matches at the 40,000-capacity{{Cite web |title=Instalaciones |url=http://www.realsociedad.eus/es/club/instalaciones |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=www.realsociedad.eus |language=es}} [[Anoeta Stadium]]. Real Sociedad won the Liga title in [[1980–81 La Liga|1980–81]] and [[1981–82 La Liga|1981–82]], and finished runner-up in [[1979–80 La Liga|1979–80]], [[1987–88 La Liga|1987–88]], and [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03]]. The club has also won the [[Copa del Rey]] four times, in [[1909 Copa del Rey|1909]], [[1986–87 Copa del Rey|1987]], [[2019–20 Copa del Rey|2020]], and [[2025–26 Copa del Rey|2026]], and the [[Spanish Super Cup]] once, in [[1982 Supercopa de España|1982]]. It contests the [[Basque derby]] against rivals [[Athletic Bilbao]]. Real Sociedad was a founding member of [[La Liga]] in 1929; its longest spell in the top flight was for 40 seasons, from 1967 to 2007.{{cite web |url=http://free-elements.com/Spain/Goals/Res/Res5.html |title=Real Sociedad |work=free-elements.com |access-date=2011-12-22 |archive-date=2023-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230813203507/http://free-elements.com/Spain/Goals/Res/Res5.html |url-status=live }} The club has competed in the European Cup / [[UEFA Champions League]] five times, between the [[1981–82 European Cup|1981–82]] and [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|2023–24]] editions. Traditionally the club followed a policy ([[Athletic Bilbao signing policy|similar to that of its rival Athletic]]) of signing only Basque players, before signing [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Irish]] forward [[John Aldridge]] in 1989. While a strong Basque contingent has been retained among its players, nowadays both non-Basque Spaniards and foreign players are represented at the club. Its [[Real Sociedad cantera|youth academy]] subsequent to the all-Basque era has still been very successful in developing internationally renowned players, including [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] winners [[Xabi Alonso]], [[Antoine Griezmann]],[https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55405431 Athletic Bilbao v Real Sociedad: How La Real's trust in youth is paying off] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425162303/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55405431 |date=2021-04-25 }}, Alex Bysouth, [[BBC Sport]], 29 December 2020 [[Mikel Oyarzabal]] and [[Martin Zubimendi]].[https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6400637/2025/06/03/arsenal-zubimendi-transfer-update-real-sociedad/ Arsenal target Martin Zubimendi expecting long summer as he prepares to leave Real Sociedad], Nnamdi Onyeagwara, [[The Athletic]], 3 June 2025 Aside from football (including a [[Real Sociedad Femenino|women's team]]), Real Sociedad also has several sections in other sports, including [[track and field]], [[field hockey]], and [[Basque pelota]]."}}
